headline: European troops join France's Bastille Day parade

sources.title: France's Bastille Day parade showcases European support for Ukraine
France flaunts firepower and unity with allies as Macron hosts final Bastille Day parade
European troops join Paris Bastille Day parade in show of unity for Ukraine
Ukraine Troops March Through Paris As Macron, Starmer & European Leaders Watch Bastille Day (video, The Financial Express)

chunks.text: Every year on July 14, France celebrates Bastille Day, the country's national day. This year, France {{put on}} its yearly military [[parade]] down the famous Champs-Élysées [[avenue]] in Paris. [[Soldiers]], [[tanks]], and planes moved slowly along the wide street while huge [[crowds]] {{turned up}} to watch. The holiday {{looks back}} at [[a key moment]] in French history and gives the whole nation [[a chance to]] feel [[proud]].

verbs.correct: To organize and present a public event or show
verbs.wrong: To suggest a plan for others to think about
verbs.why: Theaters put on a play for the whole town, and cities put on fireworks shows every summer. France puts on a military parade down the Champs-Élysées every year for Bastille Day.

verbs.correct: To arrive or come to a place in large numbers
verbs.wrong: To be found by chance after having been lost
verbs.why: Fans turn up hours early for a big concert, and neighbors turn up for a block party even in the rain. Huge crowds turned up along the Champs-Élysées this year to watch the parade.

verbs.correct: To think about something that happened in the past
verbs.wrong: To study or examine something in careful detail
verbs.why: People look back on their school days with a smile, and a class reunion lets old friends look back together. This holiday lets the French look back at a key moment in their history and feel proud of it.

chunks.text: This year's parade was different from all the others. [[For the first time]], [[troops]] from other European countries {{joined in}} and marched together with the French army. The event was planned to {{stand up for}} Ukraine, which has been fighting a war against Russia for years. Through the parade, these nations wanted to {{show off}} their [[unity]] and [[prove]] to Ukraine that it is [[not alone]].

verbs.correct: To join an activity with other people
verbs.wrong: To officially become a member of the army
verbs.why: Neighbors join in a street festival, and new students join in a game at recess. This year, soldiers from other European countries joined in the French parade for the first time.

verbs.correct: To defend or support someone or something
verbs.wrong: To bravely oppose and confront a powerful enemy
verbs.why: Good friends stand up for each other in an argument, and a lawyer can stand up for someone who has no voice. This year's parade was planned to stand up for Ukraine during its long war with Russia.

verbs.correct: To proudly display something you are proud of
verbs.wrong: To pretend to have skills you do not really have
verbs.why: Athletes show off their medals after a big win, and homeowners show off a new garden to the whole street. Through the parade, these nations wanted to show off their unity and prove Ukraine is not alone.

chunks.text: Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, was invited as a [[guest of honor]] and {{looked on}} from a special [[stand]]. A small group of Ukrainian soldiers {{marched past}} while proudly carrying their national flag. Two Ukrainian [[pilots]], who had trained in France, flew [[fighter jets]] over the crowd. [[In total]], about 6,800 troops {{took part}}, setting [[a new record]].

verbs.correct: To watch something as an observer only
verbs.wrong: To guard and keep someone safe by watching them
verbs.why: Neighbors look on as workers repair a broken water pipe, and people nearby look on when a street performer starts a show. Zelenskyy looked on from a special stand as the parade passed in front of him.

verbs.correct: To walk past a place in a formal group
verbs.wrong: To move to the very front and lead a parade
verbs.why: Soldiers march past a saluting officer during a ceremony, and students march past their families at graduation. A small group of Ukrainian soldiers marched past while proudly carrying their national flag.

verbs.correct: To be involved in an activity or event
verbs.wrong: To happen or occur at a particular place
verbs.why: Volunteers take part in a charity run, and students take part in a school play. About 6,800 troops took part in this year's parade, setting a new record for the event.

chunks.text: For President Emmanuel Macron, this was a special day. It was his last Bastille Day parade before he {{steps down}} as president next year. Around 30 world leaders {{showed up}} to [[stand beside]] him. A heat wave was so strong that many towns had to {{call off}} their [[fireworks]], but the [[mood]] in Paris stayed proud and strong.

verbs.correct: To leave an important job or position
verbs.wrong: To get involved in order to help
verbs.why: A tired coach might step down at the end of the season, and a company founder can step down to let new leaders take charge. Macron will step down as president next year after his final term ends.

verbs.correct: To arrive or appear at a place
verbs.wrong: To guide a visitor around a place
verbs.why: Guests show up early for a wedding, and old classmates show up at a reunion after many years. Around 30 world leaders showed up in Paris to stand beside Macron for his final parade.

verbs.correct: To cancel something that was planned
verbs.wrong: To make something bigger or more exciting
verbs.why: Airlines call off flights during a storm, and organizers call off an outdoor concert when lightning strikes. Some French towns had to call off their fireworks this year because of a bad heat wave.

mainIdea.s: For the first time, troops from other European countries joined in and marched with France. The march stood up for Ukraine, and it was the French president's last parade before he steps down.
mainIdea.why: European troops joined in and marched with France for the first time, to stand up for Ukraine. This was also the French president's last Bastille Day parade before he steps down.

mainIdea.s: Ukrainian troops led this year's military parade, while French soldiers looked on from the stand. Ukraine's leader put on the show to prove Ukraine could run it without France's help.
mainIdea.why: Close, but France's own army led the parade as usual, and only a small group of Ukrainian soldiers marched past. Ukraine's leader was a guest of honor who looked on from the stand, not the organizer.

mainIdea.s: Each summer, Paris also hosts a separate air show where nations sell new fighter jets to buyers. This year's event drew top executives from major plane makers hoping to sign new deals.
mainIdea.why: This is about a separate Paris air show where countries sell fighter jets to buyers. It is not about the Bastille Day parade or support for Ukraine.

tf.s: France had to call off the whole parade because of the heat wave.
tf.why: False. The heat wave meant some towns called off their fireworks, but the parade still went ahead.

tf.s: Troops from other European countries joined in and marched with the French army.
tf.why: For the first time, troops from other European countries joined in and marched together with the French army.

tf.s: President Macron will step down as president next year.
tf.why: It was his last Bastille Day parade before he steps down as president next year.

tf.s: Only a few people turned up to watch the parade.
tf.why: Huge crowds turned up to watch the parade along the Champs-Élysées.

tf.s: Zelenskyy looked on from a special stand as a guest of honor.
tf.why: Ukraine's president was invited as a guest of honor and looked on from a special stand.

tf.s: The European nations wanted to show off their disagreement with each other.
tf.why: They wanted to show off their unity, not any disagreement.

lines.text: Did you see the pictures from Bastille Day? France {{put on}} its big parade in Paris, but this year was special.
For the first time, troops from other European countries {{joined in}} and marched with the French army. About 6,800 soldiers {{took part}}, a new record.
The parade was planned to {{stand up for}} Ukraine. The countries wanted to {{show off}} their unity and prove Ukraine isn't alone.
[[Guest of honor]]. He {{looked on}} from a special stand while Ukrainian soldiers {{marched past}} with their flag. Two Ukrainian pilots flew fighter jets over the crowd.
Huge crowds {{turned up}} along the avenue, and about 30 world leaders {{showed up}} to stand beside Macron.
Yes, his final Bastille Day before he {{steps down}}. The holiday {{looks back}} at French history, so it was an emotional one.
Only the heat. It was so strong that many towns had to {{call off}} their fireworks. Paris kept the mood proud anyway.
